question: How do Morgan Stanley, Merrill and Raymond James each approach advisor recruiting and retention?

claims.text: Recruiting - Morgan Stanley: On the 1Q25 earnings call (April 2025), CEO Ted Pick said people are "coming toward the platform". He tied this to a funnel that works and to the financial advisor seeing the integrated firm, which he said offers access to intellectual capital, technology and "compensation that is viewed to be fair and motivating". He said the firm is selective and is getting a lot of inbound inquiry.

Recruiting - Morgan Stanley: On the 2Q25 call (July 2025), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said the firm has "a great platform" and recruits interested in what it has been investing in. She said advisor-led recruiting sits alongside flows from workplace, so net new assets show strength in all three channels.

Recruiting - Merrill: On the 4Q25 call (published January 2026), Bank of America CFO Alastair Borthwick said Merrill advisors see the value of the franchise. He said the firm is "picking up the recruiting of experienced advisors" but that this "isn't an enormous part of our strategy". He also described a training program for wealth management as something the firm can keep driving to improve net new flows. The chunk is from the GWIM segment call but names Merrill FAs.

Recruiting - Merrill: Merrill's Advisor Development Program web page (content as of 2026-11-03, undated) lays out an in-house route to becoming an advisor. Entry roles require the SIE, Series 7 and Series 66 licences, last approximately 13 months, and lead to the ADP Financial Advisor stage (approximately 1-4 years) and then Merrill Core Advisor (FA). One path works in a Bank of America Financial Center or Merrill office.

Recruiting - Merrill: Trade press (published 2026-11-16; indicative only) reports that Merrill added advisors from UBS, Morgan Stanley and Edward Jones in recent weeks. It says Merrill executives in October touted that recruited assets to the wealth unit doubled year-over-year. It also says the firm largely pulled back from veteran broker recruiting at the end of 2017 and returned under Co-Presidents Lindsay Hans and Eric Schimpf, who took over in 2023 and restored a focus on hiring and a more aggressive offer.

Recruiting - Raymond James: On the fiscal 3Q25 call (October 2025), CEO Paul Shoukry said the firm ended the fiscal year with a record number of financial advisors, 2% higher than the prior year. He credited "solid advisor retention as well as strong recruiting results" and cited a robust recruiting pipeline. He described a "best-of-both-worlds" value proposition of culture plus leading technology, and said the firm's balance sheet and commitment to independence differentiate it. He said the firm continues to invest in its platform to retain and attract advisors.

Recruiting - Raymond James: The fiscal 2025 10-K (published 2025-11-25) calls continuous recruitment and retention of financial advisors "an important driver of our success". It attributes the ability to attract advisors to the firm's values-based culture, commitment to service and the unique ways it serves advisors. Aspiring advisors can enter through the Wealth Management Associate Program or the Advisor Mastery Program.

Recruiting - Raymond James: The firm's recruiting page (page content as of 2026-04-21) presents AdvisorChoice®, with five affiliation options: Traditional Employee, Advisor Select, Independent Contractor, Bank & Credit Union, and Corporate RIA. The page describes Traditional Employee as offering "book ownership".

Recruiting - Raymond James: Trade press (WealthManagement.com, published 2026-10-29; indicative only) reports that Shoukry said trailing 12-month production of recruited advisors joining the domestic independent contractor and employee channels was $538 million, up from $407 million the prior year. It says those advisors represented more than $82 billion in client assets. It also reports Shoukry saying recruiting success is spread across all affiliation channels, including RIA custody.

Retention - Raymond James: The fiscal 2025 10-K (published 2025-11-25) describes a department dedicated to growth-oriented tools and resources, including business coaching, for its financial advisors. It also describes national conferences for the employee and independent contractor advisor channels, each attended by thousands of advisors each year.

Retention - Raymond James: The 10-Q for the period ended 2026-06-30 (published 2026-08-05) says the firm offers loans to prospective financial advisors "for recruiting and retention purposes". The offers are contingent on the individuals joining or continuing their affiliation, and unfunded commitments for these loans were $14 million as of June 30, 2026.

adjacent.text: The Morgan Stanley 10-K for 2025 (published 2026-02-19) says talent development programs for employees are designed to help them achieve career goals, and that the firm believes supporting employee development "contributes to long-term retention".
adjacent.differs_because: It covers all employees, not specifically financial advisors, so it is not Morgan Stanley's advisor retention approach.

adjacent.text: On the 4Q24 call (January 2025), Ted Pick said Morgan Stanley retains 99% of its clients.
adjacent.differs_because: This is client retention, not advisor retention.

adjacent.text: Trade press (InvestmentNews, published 2026-10-26) reports that Morgan Stanley and Merrill Lynch are not introducing retention bonuses in their 2027 advisor pay plans, "adhering to a more traditional approach". It says Morgan Stanley is raising a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027 and Merrill is leaving its core pay grid unchanged.
adjacent.differs_because: Trade-press reporting is indicative, not authoritative.

adjacent.text: Bank of America's investor day deck (published 2025-11-05) shows GWIM, covering Merrill and the Private Bank, with more than 15K wealth advisors.
adjacent.differs_because: GWIM includes both Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank; the two have different reporting scopes, so GWIM figures are not Merrill's.

gaps.what: Retention - Morgan Stanley: not found in the evidence provided. The evidence has no Morgan Stanley statement on how it retains financial advisors specifically.
gaps.suggested_source: Morgan Stanley earnings call transcripts, Wealth Management investor presentations, or advisor compensation disclosures

gaps.what: Retention - Merrill: not found in the evidence provided. The evidence has no Merrill statement on how it retains advisors.
gaps.suggested_source: Bank of America earnings calls and GWIM investor materials, or Merrill advisor programme documents

gaps.what: Merrill does not report standalone results.
gaps.suggested_source: Bank of America GWIM segment disclosures in the 10-K and earnings materials

gaps.what: Neither firm discloses advisor attrition on a comparable basis.
gaps.suggested_source: Company disclosures of advisor departures, or industry recruiting data
